title: Echo: Graph-Enhanced Retrieval and Execution Feedback for Issue Reproduction Test Generation
datasets: SWT-Bench-Lite (276 mentioned as benchmark context; not Echo primary evaluation)
task: Generate issue reproducing test for SWT-Bench; retrieval → candidate patch → test generation → automatic execution → semantic verification → dual-version check/refinement.
input_setting: GitHub issue, repository and code graph; retrieve focal code and three regression tests, use Prometheus candidate fix as additional context/oracle, generate separate test file, execute in Docker and validate against original and candidate-patched versions.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper §9 Data Availability explicitly names EuniAI/Echo for code/results/logs; repository README and module names identify Echo and match the six-stage pipeline.
license: Paper states CC BY 4.0; repository GitHub API license=null and no root LICENSE found, so software license is unverified.
exact_models: Public example.env at checked commit defaults both PROMETHEUS_ADVANCED_MODEL and PROMETHEUS_BASE_MODEL to gpt-4o; model configuration does not match the paper setting without override.
weights_status: No fine-tuning/weights. Gemini 2.5 Pro is hosted API; source supports Google model integration. Paid API required to regenerate results.
evaluation_route: Public app includes LangGraph issue-reproduction and graph retrieval code, Docker management, Neo4j graph, dataset loading and JSON prediction persistence; README requires Python 3.11+, Docker, Neo4j, PostgreSQL and model credentials. No repo-root tests/, predictions/, logs/ or results/ were present in pinned tree (101 entries), despite paper Data Availability claiming results and all logs. No execution or API call performed.
blockers: Paper model Gemini 2.5 Pro / temp 0.5 differs from tracked example.env default of GPT-4o for both advanced/base model roles; exact experiment configuration and component-to-model mapping unavailable.

Paper reports 433 Verified tasks; 419 were processed and 287 successes. It says 14 skipped due to a 500-step limit; per-project Table 3 has 419 processed and 433 total. Cached per-instance output needed to inspect skipped/failed cohort, but claimed results/logs are absent from the public repository tree at the checked commit.
Repo has no license metadata/root LICENSE, no lockfile (pyproject has several unpinned dependency ranges), and requires a heavyweight Docker + Neo4j + PostgreSQL stack.
Paper cost table reports $1.54 per instance and reports only one stochastic run at temperature 0.5. Full 433-instance replay would be about $667.82 at the reported average (estimate, not spent).

Paper uses a Prometheus-generated candidate patch as an oracle for dual-version feedback and itself cautions that candidate patches can be incorrect; final reliability depends on this imperfect oracle.
Paper describes graph-enhanced cross-file dependency retrieval, but tracked graph edge types are only file/AST/parent/text/chunk; no explicit call/import edges were found in graph type definitions.
concept_fit: High: retrieves issue-relevant code/tests, plans/executes fail-to-pass tests and uses issue, test and execution evidence; candidate patch provides an imperfect behavioral oracle. The graph appears structural rather than explicit call/data-flow semantics, based on tracked edge types.
recommendation: Good concept-aligned related work, but not the easiest faithful reproduction candidate. Source is public, while the exact Gemini configuration, experiment outputs and logs are not in the checked repo; missing software license and heavy services add friction. Use as a conceptual baseline for query/context retrieval and dual-version oracle limitations, not as the first implementation to rerun.
supporting_locations: Paper §§4–9, Tables 1–5; full text cache SHA-256 80cf84483590cbaaf5e0efc59748f5035fcf2636eab05cda73a7fd3f197c5132
Paper cost: Table 5 $1.54 average per instance; per-instance count 433 implies approx. $667.82 only as arithmetic estimate.
